lede: Construction project manager in San Francisco. I run projects, and I write the software they're missing.

markups.label: The classroom: ten years of projects
markups.text: Ten years running regulated projects in the Bay Area: schools, a hospital campus and historic renovation. In the field, in the office and in owner meetings.

markups.label: Duct hits beam: the problem I build software for
markups.text: Duct hits beam. On a real job that becomes an RFI, maybe a change order, and a thread split across Procore and five inboxes. I build tools that track it and draft the paperwork for a person to review.

markups.label: The foundation: license and education
markups.text: Licensed California general contractor (Class B), OSHA 30, and an M.S. in Civil Engineering & Engineering Project Management from UC Berkeley.

notes: I've spent ten years on regulated projects in the Bay Area: schools, a hospital campus and historic renovation. I've worked in the field, in the office and in owner meetings.
Most of a PM's day goes into RFIs, submittals, change orders, cost reports and email, spread across Procore and a dozen inboxes. A lot of it is copy and paste.
I build tools that pull that information into one place and use AI to write first drafts. A person reviews every draft before it goes out.
Most of what I build runs on live projects and is not public. The demos on this site use fictional sample data. Ask if you'd like a walkthrough of the rest.
I'm a licensed California general contractor (Class B) with an M.S. in Civil Engineering & Engineering Project Management from UC Berkeley.
connect: Building software for construction, or need someone who understands both the jobsite and the code? Send a question the way the job would: as an RFI.
